newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper seen whippy, aluminium to climb.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper seen whippy, aluminium to climb.

text.p: Copper was expected to whip around on Thursday as an expected hefty stocks rise puts pressure on prices while tight technical conditions pull the market in the opposite way, traders and analysts said.
Aluminium was likely to try the upside after a positive close and another bounce off key support around $1,545/50 on Wednesday.
COPPER -
The market would be volatile as competing forces yanked it in opposite directions.

Fears of another big stock increase after Wednesday's 17,025-tonne rise sent prices slipping in early trade on Thursday to be indicated at $2,230/35, down from the previous afternoon kerb close of $2,267.
Below $2,230, the low of July 9, further support was pegged at $2,210 and $2,170, chartist Harry Creates of broker AMT said.

Lack of activity during the slow summer season and big tonnages being delivered into LME warehouses were pressuring the market, but near-term technical tightness was giving it a firm undertone, analysts said.
The cash/threes backwardation was still impressive, but was indicated about $30 narrower early on Thursday at $155/$165.
"We remain cautious to taking aggressive short positions as the spread remains tight," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.
But as inventories built up, the price would likely have to give way, he added.
"Should further stocks rises be noted in the coming weeks, the spread is likely to ease further, hence increasing downward pressure on the three month price," he said in a commentary.
At 0745 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,230/35, down $25 from Wednesday's late close.
ALUMINIUM -
Prices should challenge the upside after closing at their highs of $1,570 on Wednesday, but they would have difficulty breaking through the psychological $1,600 area.
"The close is somewhat constructive, pointing the market toward the high end of the summer trading range of $1,590/95," said broker Gerald in a commentary.
But weakness in copper could put a damper on any effort to climb higher.
On the upside, the 10-day moving average at $1,580 would prove an obstacle.
A move above $1,600 would put resistance at $1,606 and $1,620 into play, while on the downside, a breach of support at $1,544 could see a move to the February 11 low of $1,534.
At 0745 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,564/67, down about $9 from Wednesday's late close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
